newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Leumi in talks with two groups on Africa-Israel.
newsitem.headline: Leumi in talks with two groups on Africa-Israel.

text.p: Bank Leumi is beginning negotiations with two of the three groups that made offers for the bank's controlling stake in Africa Israel Investments, a spokeswoman for the bank said on Wednesday.

A source close to the sale of Africa, a property-development company with interests in tourism and building products, said one of the three had not made a formal bid. Instead, it had offered a letter of intent, making a bid conditional on several changes in the terms of the tender.

The bank has not revealed the names of the three, but a source confirmed reports in the local media that the two formal bids were from Lev Leviev, a leading figure in the local diamond industry, and an unnamed South African group.
Ronald Lauder, a U.S. investor and heir to the Estee Lauder fortune, together with Bear Stearns, made the conditional offer, the source said.
Talks with the first two bidders are under way and should be completed within a few days.

Leumi is selling part of its Africa stake together with the holdings of Israeli businessmen Mordechai Zisser and Eitan Wertheimer. The combined stakes are equal to 46.58 percent of equity and 54.2 percent of voting rights in the company.

The bank expects to receive substantially above the minimum company valuation of $330 million that was set in the tender. The tender is for Africa shorn of its key insurance business, which is being spun off and sold to Italian insurer Generali SpA.
Leumi, Israel's second-largest bank, must reduce its stake in Africa to 25 percent to comply with Israeli banking reforms that require banks to reduce their non-bank assets.
